title: Correct Tenant-Notice Method
description: Conservative compliance checklist capable of tenant-lawyer review; not attorney approval.

rows.label: Verify coverage
rows.value: Check exact address in SF Planning PIM; confirm exemptions
rows.notes: Exact address not supplied in this case.

rows.label: Verify license
rows.value: Current Rent Increase License on effective date
rows.notes: Tenant portal lookup.

rows.label: Verify 12 months / anniversary
rows.value: At least 12 months since last increase
rows.notes: Use rate in effect on increase date.

rows.label: Verify banked amounts
rows.value: Verify history before banking; SF.gov says 24 full months but examples conflict; add percentages, no compounding/prorating
rows.notes: No case banked amount inferred.

rows.label: Written notice timing
rows.value: 30 days; 90 days if >10% alone/combined in same year; +5 days if mailed
rows.notes: 827(c) longer notice controls.

rows.label: Notice contents
rows.value: Dollar amount, percentage, effective date; banked portion if any
rows.notes: No rounding up.

rows.label: Delivery
rows.value: Personal delivery or mail under Civil Code 827 / CCP 1013
rows.notes: Keep proof of service.

rows.label: Petition grounds
rows.value: Petition/worksheet before notice when required
rows.notes: Otherwise notice may be void.

rows.label: Neutral policy
rows.value: Identical written neutral policy, dates, calculations and recordkeeping for each eligible unit
rows.notes: Document neutral eligibility reasons if only one unit is raised.

rows.label: Legal review
rows.value: Capable of tenant-lawyer review; no approval claimed
rows.notes: Free counseling is not legal advice; TRC covers eviction proceedings.

rows.label: License before effective date; report before relying on it
rows.value: Complete Housing Inventory and confirm a current license for the unit before the increase effective date; safest practice is before serving notice.
rows.notes: Official pages require the effective-date license; no express separate pre-mailing Board notice for ordinary annual/banked increases was found.

rows.label: Keep the license record
rows.value: File the license record and a dated portal lookup with the notice and proof of service
rows.notes: Evidence if the increase is challenged.

rows.label: 90-day notice if the total exceeds 10%
rows.value: 90 days when the increase alone or combined with another increase in the same year is more than 10%
rows.notes: A correctly banked total can exceed 10%.

rows.label: Check the retaliation clock
rows.value: Review Civil Code 1942.5 triggers, timing, causation and good-faith cause exceptions before serving notice.
rows.notes: The 180-day provisions are conditional and fact-specific; not every repair request automatically bars an increase.

rows.label: Keep the fee separate
rows.value: Pay or confirm the Rent Board Fee ($59.00 per dwelling unit for 2026-2027, due March 1) and, if recovering 50%, show it as a separate fee recovery rather than folding it into the rent increase
rows.notes: The fee is not part of base rent.

rows.label: Match each notice to a license on its effective date
rows.value: Check the portal license status for the specific effective date of each notice, for each unit, including any prior year
rows.notes: A license now does not cure a notice effective before it existed.

rows.label: Re-serve rather than backdate
rows.value: If a notice went out unlicensed, report, confirm the license, and serve a new notice with a compliant effective date
rows.notes: Do not backdate or assume retroactive cure; obtain legal advice on any already-served notice.

rows.label: Check fixed-term versus periodic lease
rows.value: Fixed-term rent generally cannot be raised mid-term unless the agreement expressly allows it; periodic tenancies use statutory notice rules.
rows.notes: Actual lease type/clause unverified; no mid-term increase approved.

rows.label: One unit versus both
rows.value: No official rule found requiring both units to be raised. Apply neutral unit-based criteria and document eligibility/anniversary reasons.
rows.notes: Raising both does not immunize discrimination or retaliation; consider less discriminatory alternatives.

rows.label: Keep fee recovery separate from rent
rows.value: Up to 50% of the paid annual fee may be recovered by deposit-interest deduction or compliant bill; penalties are not recoverable.
rows.notes: Not base rent and not an ordinary rent increase; tenant nonpayment is not just cause for eviction.
